Look for. The "Pink Hat" mechanic: Identify a specific item driving disproportionate sales (e.g., 40% of revenue), remove it from the store entirely so it cannot be purchased, and make it a free gift for spending ~30-40% above the current AOV (e.g., current AOV is $65; gift unlocks at $85). Demographic layering: Moving from a $500 problem ("women over 40 finding a man") to a $10,000 problem ("divorced women over 40 avoiding another toxic relationship") to secure product-market fit.
Skip. Generic advice to "give away a free tote bag" (the gift must be highly coveted, not cheap swag).
Scope mix. 10% baseline (understanding demographics), 90% growth (weaponizing inventory to force AOV jumps).
Goes here. Financial formulas for evaluating traffic scalability, calculating baseline traffic break-even points, and modeling Lifetime Gross Profit (LTV) versus Day-1 acquisition cost.

why: Shifts focus from Day-1 CAC to 12-month Lifetime Gross Profit and establishes the exact "Revenue per 100 Visitors" mathematical benchmark required to scale cold traffic.
topics: [traffic scalability formulas, lifetime gross profit, CAC vs LTV modeling]

Topics. profit and contribution formulas / 12-month Lifetime Gross Profit vs. Day-1 profit; traffic math / the "Revenue per 100 Visitors" formula combining Conversion Rate and Average Order Value (AOV).

Look for. The strict traffic scalability formula: Conversion Rate x AOV >= 300. (Example: 3% conversion rate x $100 AOV = 300, which equals $300 in revenue per 100 visitors). A metric below 300 indicates cold traffic cannot be scaled profitably given average CPCs. The 12-month profit model: Accepting a $20 loss on first purchase ($60 CAC for $40 gross profit) to secure $400 in backend gross profit over the next 12 months.
Skip. Generic complaints about rising ad costs or basic definitions of CAC.
Scope mix. 100% baseline (the mathematical rules for scaling ad spend).

The AI Bot Workflow: Bot logs into ad accounts -> identifies top KPIs -> checks competitor ad libraries for top performers -> feeds data into AI UGC software to generate variations -> drops files in Google Drive -> pings media buyer.

Topics. list growth / utilizing 3rd-party identity resolution (e.g., OpenSend) to capture US traffic; survey mechanics / open-ended questioning incentivized by guaranteed rewards; onboarding / daily habit-formation messaging.

Look for. Anonymous identity resolution mechanics: Utilizing network-wide certificates (where a user opted in on another site) to legally send cold emails to website visitors who abandoned before entering their email. Survey incentivization: Using "everyone wins" models (e.g., entry for a $1,000 gift card, plus a guaranteed $30 store credit for completing it) to extract open-ended objections and product requests. Habit-stacking flows: Sending emails every single day for the first 90 days to force product consumption (e.g., requesting daily hair-loss progress photos) until it becomes a permanent habit.

Scope mix. 30% baseline (surveys), 70% growth (anonymous identity resolution).
